pairs: Quid habet amplius homo de universo labore suo quo laborat sub sole?
What more does a man have from all his labor, as he labors under the sun?
gyrat per meridiem, et flectitur ad aquilonem.
it circles through the south, and arcs toward the north.
Lustrans universa in circuitu pergit spiritus,
The spirit continues on, illuminating everything in its circuit,
and turning again in its cycle.
All rivers enter into the sea,
and the sea does not overflow.
ad locum unde exeunt flumina revertuntur ut iterum fluant.
To the place from which the rivers go out, they return, so that they may flow again.
non potest eas homo explicare sermone.
man is not able to explain them with words.
The eye is not satisfied by seeing,
nor is the ear fulfilled by hearing.
What is it that has existed?
The same shall exist in the future.
What is it that has been done?
The same shall continue to be done.
There is nothing new under the sun.
Neither is anyone able to say:
jam enim præcessit in sæculis quæ fuerunt ante nos.
For it has already been brought forth in the ages that were before us.
There is no remembrance of the former things.
sed nec eorum quidem quæ postea futura sunt erit recordatio apud eos qui futuri sunt in novissimo.
Indeed, neither shall there be any record of past things in the future, for those who will exist at the very end.
Ego Ecclesiastes fui rex Israël in Jerusalem;
I, Ecclesiastes, was king of Israel at Jerusalem.
et proposui in animo meo quærere
And I was determined in my mind to seek and to investigate wisely,
et investigare sapienter de omnibus quæ fiunt sub sole.
concerning all that is done under the sun.
Hanc occupationem pessimam dedit Deus filiis hominum,
God has given this very difficult task to the sons of men,
so that they may be occupied by it.
Vidi cuncta quæ fiunt sub sole,
I have seen all that is done under the sun,
all is emptiness and an affliction of the spirit.
The perverse are unwilling to be corrected,
and the number of the foolish is boundless.
I have spoken in my heart, saying:
et præcessi omnes sapientia qui fuerunt ante me in Jerusalem;
and I have surpassed all the wise who were before me in Jerusalem.”
et mens mea contemplata est multa sapienter, et didici.
And my mind has contemplated many things wisely, and I have learned.
Dedique cor meum ut scirem prudentiam atque doctrinam,
And I have dedicated my heart, so that I may know prudence and doctrine,
and also error and foolishness. Yet I recognize that,
et agnovi quod in his quoque esset labor et afflictio spiritus:
in these things also, there is hardship, and affliction of the spirit.
eo quod in multa sapientia multa sit indignatio;
with much wisdom there is also much anger.
